as_told.title: Townsend Brown's Winterhaven proposal cites Heaviside gravity

plain: The claim is that a 1953 plan written by the inventor Thomas Townsend Brown, known as the Winter Haven proposal after the Florida town, describes the same kind of program that insiders today say the US runs to study and build UFO-like craft. Brown studied how electric charge might create a pushing force, which his followers link to controlling gravity. Michels makes the claim himself in a documentary about Brown, saying the 1953 proposal 'almost exactly resembles how all insiders describe America's secret UFO program.' His co-host Jack, who goes by an alias and says he works in defense and aerospace, brings it up in a later episode. He adds that in the proposal Brown 'says Oliver Heaviside had a very adequate theory of gravity back in the 1890s and we would be right to listen to him.' Heaviside was a British physicist. Neither teller quotes the proposal's own words on how the work should be organized, so how closely it matches today's insider accounts rests on Michels' reading. If he is right, the outline of a secret gravity program was on paper by 1953.
